platform: macOS 26.5 (25F71), arm64, Apple Silicon, APFS; debug build 4fecdc8 with embedded frontend, WKWebView through the test bridge
method: One isolated instance, started with an extra variable M2_04_PLANTED_SECRET in its environment. Settings' Worktree tools are driven through their DOM (values set, buttons clicked). Worktrees B to E are made with the git CLI as a user would outside the app; ages are set with utimes (ten days back). Native commands are called through the Tauri IPC only for the refusals the UI cannot ask for. The folder dialog and the confirmation boxes go through the IPC trace; every plugin:dialog call is recorded.

surface.note: One command prepares this worktree (dependencies, builds). It runs only when you click, is bounded to 2,000 characters and ten minutes, and never starts on its own.

defects.what: Cancel setup kills only the `sh` process: a command with more than one step (here `sleep 27; echo …`, as `npm install && …` would be) keeps its running child, the UI stays on "Running setup…" and reports "cancelled" only when that child ends (the output pipes stay open). The same kill is used for the ten-minute timeout.
defects.where: src-tauri/src/git.rs run_worktree_setup, #[cfg(not(target_os = "windows"))] branch: Command::new("sh") without a process group, child.kill() on cancel and timeout, then reader.join() on the inherited pipes.
defects.platform: the non-Windows code path (macOS and Linux)

defects.what: The setup command inherits the app's whole environment (a variable planted in the app's environment is visible to it); the roadmap's "purges the inherited environment" does not match the code (no env_clear).

proposedMacosState.M2-04: ◐ (verdicts pass; cancellation of a multi-step command is not effective on the non-Windows path)

notProved: M2-06 persistent cleanup intent resumed after an interruption: muse-desktop.worktree-cleanup.v1 is loaded and saved by useMuseSessions but nothing writes an intent and no Retry cleanup action exists at 08b291d, so there is nothing to resume.
limits: The ten-minute kill (timedOut) is not waited for; it is covered by the Rust tests only.
